description: Human-curated keyword decisions supporting source-signal mapping version 2026-07-29-v2.9.

1920s.rationale: Potentially useful period metadata, but held for manual review because adding it displaced stronger title themes under the current per-dimension limit.

1960s.rationale: Potentially useful period metadata, but held for manual review because adding it displaced stronger title themes under the current per-dimension limit.

1970s.rationale: Potentially useful period metadata, but held for manual review because adding it displaced stronger title themes under the current per-dimension limit.

19th century.rationale: Potentially useful period metadata, but held for manual review because adding it displaced stronger title themes under the current per-dimension limit.

absurdism.rationale: The reviewed titles consistently use it as an absurdist-tone cue, but not necessarily as comedy.

action.rationale: Action is already represented by canonical genre metadata and is too broad to infer pacing by itself.

alcoholism.rationale: The concept is potentially useful, but the current taxonomy has no precise addiction or substance-use value and family/background prominence varies by title.

alien invasion.rationale: Across the affected titles it consistently indicates conflict with an alien force; the existing broad alien-encounter value is a conservative fit.

android.rationale: The reviewed titles use android consistently as a robotics and technology-story cue.

angry.rationale: The keyword does not distinguish character emotion from the overall viewing mood reliably.

anthology.rationale: Anthology describes series format rather than viewing tone or theme.

anxious.rationale: Across the reviewed titles it is a stable tense-mood cue.

audacious.rationale: A conservative alias of the existing bold tone.

awestruck.rationale: The affected titles do not support one stable mood interpretation across the catalog.

based on video game.rationale: Adaptation provenance is factual metadata, not a viewing signal.

best picture nominee.rationale: Award status is marketing/provenance metadata and not a viewing signal.

biography.rationale: The provider keyword spans crime, historical and adjacent works and does not safely imply one existing audience value.

boston massachusetts.rationale: A geographic setting must not be forced into topic or mood.

bounty hunter.rationale: A stable story archetype across several titles that may later support a character-archetype or story-premise taxonomy; no suitable current dimension exists.

cerebral.rationale: The broad cue crowded more specific tone and mood signals in the reviewed titles.

cyberpunk.rationale: A stable multi-title subgenre with clear discovery value.

dark.rationale: A direct and stable alias of the existing dark tone.

death of daughter.rationale: The phrase reveals a specific consequential family death.

death of husband.rationale: The phrase reveals a specific consequential family death.

depressing.rationale: A stable bleak-mood cue in the reviewed title set.

disturbed.rationale: A stable unsettling-mood cue in the reviewed title set.

england.rationale: A geographic setting must not be forced into topic or mood.

fall from grace.rationale: The phrase may reveal a major character arc outcome.

family relationships.rationale: A stable family-dynamics cue using established family and character-drama values.

female protagonist.rationale: A protagonist attribute is factual role metadata and does not imply one viewing signal.

gloomy.rationale: The cue conflicted with stronger existing moods in the reviewed title set.

harsh.rationale: The affected titles use it inconsistently as setting, subject, or reaction language, so it does not support one stable mood or tone.

hero.rationale: The broad character-role noun does not produce a stable viewer-facing signal.

historical.rationale: The broad keyword supports only a low-confidence period-setting cue, not historical drama.

hopeless.rationale: A stable bleak-mood cue in the reviewed title set.

horrified.rationale: The provider adjective can describe audience reaction or subject matter and does not reliably identify the title's overall mood.

husband wife relationship.rationale: A marital relationship is a neutral family relationship cue and does not imply strain.

inspirational.rationale: The keyword supports an inspiring mood but does not guarantee an uplifting tone.

introspective.rationale: A stable contemplative and thoughtful viewing cue.

kaiju.rationale: The affected titles consistently use it for a giant-creature threat, without proving that the whole title is creature-driven or high intensity.

lgbt.rationale: Identity representation should not be collapsed into conflict, mood or a generic audience expectation.

london england.rationale: A geographic setting must not be forced into topic or mood.

los angeles california.rationale: A geographic setting must not be forced into topic or mood.

loss of loved one.rationale: The phrase may reveal a consequential death or loss.

manipulation.rationale: The keyword directly supports an explicit manipulation theme but not an inferred mood.

marvel cinematic universe mcu.rationale: Franchise membership is not an audience-expectation signal.

miniseries.rationale: Series format belongs to canonical lifecycle metadata.

mother son relationship.rationale: A stable family-dynamics cue using established values.

motherhood.rationale: Across the reviewed titles it is a stable family-relationship theme, while emotional tone varies.

murder investigation.rationale: A direct alias of the established investigation-led concept.

new mexico.rationale: A geographic setting must not be forced into topic or mood.

new york city.rationale: A geographic setting must not be forced into topic or mood.

obsession.rationale: The keyword directly supports an obsession theme but does not imply an intense mood.

oscar winner.rationale: Award status is marketing/provenance metadata and not a viewing signal.

palace intrigue.rationale: The affected titles consistently center court politics and political power, but the keyword alone does not require a tense mood.

parent child relationship.rationale: A stable family-dynamics cue using established values.

parenting.rationale: The affected titles use it as a stable family-relationship theme without consistently implying conflict or a particular tone.

patriarchy.rationale: The keyword is a meaningful social concept, but the current taxonomy lacks a precise value and mapping it to generic power struggle would lose specificity.

philosophical.rationale: The broad cue displaced more specific title tone signals and needs a future taxonomy-capacity review.

philosophy.rationale: The broad cue displaced more specific title tone signals and needs a future taxonomy-capacity review.

police procedural.rationale: A stable investigation-led story pattern using established values.

possession.rationale: Across the affected titles it consistently identifies a supernatural-story element without proving horror intensity.

prequel.rationale: Franchise chronology does not describe viewing tone, mood or theme.

reboot.rationale: Reboot describes franchise and release lifecycle rather than a stable viewing signal.

rescue.rationale: A direct alias of the existing rescue-mission concept.

royal family.rationale: The phrase can be factual subject metadata and does not by itself prove court politics, conflict, or a particular viewing tone.

somber.rationale: Across the affected titles it is a stable subdued mood cue that conservatively reuses the existing melancholy value.

surrealism.rationale: A stable surreal and reality-bending viewing cue.

thoughtful.rationale: The provider adjective is broad and crowded more specific title moods under current display limits.

tragedy.rationale: A direct alias of the existing tragic mood.

villain.rationale: The broad character-role noun does not produce a stable viewer-facing signal.

war crimes.rationale: The affected titles consistently foreground the human cost of conflict; the mapping avoids inferring a specific war, period, or display warning.

anti corruption.rationale: On Dhootha the keyword directly identifies opposition to corruption; the existing corruption-story value preserves that meaning without inferring mood or tone.

clinical.rationale: Across The Pitt and The Wire, clinical can describe medical subject matter or an observational style, so it is not a stable standalone watch signal.

complicated.rationale: Across The Pitt, The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King, and The Sandman, the adjective is too vague to identify a consistent viewing quality.

drama.rationale: Drama is already represented by canonical genre metadata and is too broad to create a useful source signal.

dramatic.rationale: The provider adjective appears across materially different dramas and does not establish a stable tone, mood, or intensity.

hospital.rationale: The Pitt uses hospital as a central medical-workplace identity rather than incidental geography; the mapping is narrow and reusable for future hospital-centered titles.

informative.rationale: Across The Pitt, Blade Runner 2049, and The Wire, informative does not consistently identify the title's subject, tone, or viewing style.

medical drama.rationale: The phrase directly communicates The Pitt's medical-drama format and is precise enough to remain useful across future titles.

medical procedural.rationale: The phrase directly identifies The Pitt's medical-procedural structure without inferring pace, mood, or intensity.

pittsburgh pennsylvania.rationale: The phrase is geographic metadata and should not become a viewing signal.

real time.rationale: The phrase directly identifies The Pitt's real-time narrative structure; it is represented without inferring that the title is fast-paced.

yellow journalism.rationale: Dhootha uses the phrase as journalism subject matter, but the current taxonomy has no precise media-ethics value and broader mappings would overstate its role.

concert film.rationale: On Stop Making Sense the phrase directly identifies both the viewing format and a live music performance; these meanings remain stable for future uses of the exact keyword.

energetic.rationale: The keyword directly describes Stop Making Sense's viewing mood and can be reused without implying pacing.

love triangle.rationale: The phrase reliably identifies a romantic connection but does not reliably establish a romantic-drama genre; Materialists receives its stronger audience identity through a title override.

reincarnation.rationale: Across Eega and Avatar: The Last Airbender, the keyword consistently identifies reincarnation as a story theme without establishing mood, tone, or pace.

slice of life.rationale: The phrase is useful but can describe comedy, animation, family stories, or drama; no existing neutral canonical value represents it without over-inferring genre. Train Dreams retains its supported identity through a title override.

addiction.rationale: Sound of Metal and The Queen's Gambit both use the keyword for a central addiction subject; the mapping deliberately does not infer recovery, mood, or caution severity.

based on play or musical.rationale: This describes adaptation provenance rather than a viewing signal and must not be confused with the musical genre.

busan south korea.rationale: This is geographic metadata and is not forced into a topic or audience signal.

cautionary.rationale: Across Barbie, The Return of the King, The Wire, and A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, the adjective does not identify a stable mood, tone, or audience expectation.

cold war.rationale: Deutschland and The Americans both use the term as stable historical-political story context.

comedy horror.rationale: Bugonia and Widow's Bay both use the exact term as a stable horror-comedy genre expectation.

compassionate.rationale: The keyword spans 28 Years Later, A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms, Fargo, Inside Out, and Moon Knight and does not reliably describe the overall mood or tone.

duty.rationale: Das Boot, Godzilla Minus One, and Saving Private Ryan consistently use the keyword as a responsibility-and-service theme.

italy.rationale: The country name is geographic metadata and is not forced into a topic signal.

kidnapping.rationale: The keyword is explicit premise material in Bugonia, a later revelation in Get Out, and a secondary or undisclosed plot detail in Inception and The Silence of the Lambs. Mixed disclosure makes both global display and global spoiler suppression too broad.

mental illness.rationale: Bugonia, Joker, and The Holdovers all use the term as mental-health subject matter; the neutral existing value avoids diagnostic, mood, or danger claims.

modern history.rationale: Across Babylon Berlin, Peaky Blinders, and The Queen's Gambit, the term is broad period metadata and does not identify one stable product concept.

musical.rationale: La La Land and Main Vaapas Aaunga both use the keyword as a direct musical-format expectation.

nostalgic.rationale: The mood term is semantically valid, but mapping it globally suppresses stronger metadata fallback identity on a sparsely mapped animated title. Existing curated titles retain supported nostalgia through overrides until fallback composition can preserve both.

osaka japan.rationale: This is geographic metadata and is not forced into a story-theme signal.

power politics.rationale: Bugonia and The Wire both use the phrase for institutional power conflict; the established power-struggle value is sufficient without inferring genre or tension.

racism.rationale: 13th, Django Unchained, Get Out, and Killers of the Flower Moon all use racism as substantive subject matter rather than incidental metadata.

rio de janeiro.rationale: The city name is geographic metadata and is not promoted to a source signal.

road movie.rationale: Central Station uses the exact keyword as a journey structure and road-story identity; unlike the broader road-trip rule, this mapping does not infer an easygoing mood.

sacrifice.rationale: For the affected fantasy, superhero, and folk-horror titles, the term can disclose a decisive character outcome or ritual plot development.

slavery.rationale: 13th, Django Unchained, Gladiator, and RRR all use enslavement as substantive historical or social subject matter.

struggle for survival.rationale: Grave of the Fireflies, Society of the Snow, and The Martian consistently use the phrase for a survival premise; the existing survival-story value avoids extra pace or intensity inference.

true crime.rationale: Delhi Crime, Killers of the Flower Moon, and MINDHUNTER all use the phrase as a stable factual-crime viewing expectation, whether documentary-inspired or dramatized.

undercover.rationale: The Americans and The Departed both use the keyword for a central infiltration premise without requiring a mood or pacing inference.

washington dc usa.rationale: The city/country phrase is geographic metadata and is not promoted to a story signal.
